headline: Tariff-recovery windfall masks a still-soft top line
summary_short: Nike's fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter revenue was $10.97B, down 1.1% y/y, as North America wholesale growth was offset by declines in Greater China and EMEA; a $986M expected recovery of IEEPA tariffs drove gross margin to 49.2% and diluted EPS to $0.72.
summary_long: Revenue fell 1.1% y/y to $10.97B (-4% currency-neutral) as North America wholesale growth was offset by declines in Greater China and EMEA; NIKE Direct fell 7% on weaker digital and store traffic. Gross margin rose 890bp to 49.2%, almost entirely a $986M benefit from the expected recovery of IEEPA import tariffs the Supreme Court ruled unauthorized in February 2026. SG&A fell 2% to $4.08B on lower brand marketing. Tax rate dropped to 19.6% from 33.6% on stock-based compensation and prior-year one-offs. Net income rose 407% to $1.07B; diluted EPS was $0.72, including a $0.52 tariff-recovery benefit. Full-year revenue was flat at $46.4B; EPS fell 3% to $2.10. Cash and short-term investments were $9.0B. No numeric forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: NIKE Brand revenue was flat as North America wholesale growth offset declines in Greater China and EMEA; NIKE Direct fell 7% on lower digital and store traffic; Converse fell 32% across all territories.
Gross margin rose 890bp to 49.2%, almost entirely from an expected $986M recovery of IEEPA import tariffs after the Supreme Court ruled the tariffs unauthorized in February 2026.
Operating income benefited from the same tariff-driven gross-margin gain plus a 2% cut in SG&A, mainly lower brand marketing (demand creation -4%) and lower administrative costs.
Not broken out separately in the release; EBITDA moves with the same revenue and margin drivers disclosed for operating income above.
Net income rose alongside operating income and a lower effective tax rate (19.6% vs 33.6% a year ago), which the release attributes to stock-based compensation and prior-year one-time tax items.
EPS of $0.72 included a $0.52 per-share benefit from the expected IEEPA tariff recovery; the remainder tracks the net-income drivers above.

CEO Elliott Hill said Nike took 'decisive actions' in fiscal 2026 to reposition for long-term growth; CFO Matthew Friend called Q4 results 'in line with our expectations' amid continued challenged sell-through.
